subject: Azure Marketplace: bundling eligibility, commit thresholds, and channel margin reconciliation
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@ironbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: cloud-marketplace-ops@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on Azure bundle thresholds + partner margin

Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We finished our internal product review and have two quick gating questions before we move to drafting a PO and a Private Offer on Azure:

1) Bundled SKUs: We plan to list Redwood inference as part of a bundle (runtime + support tier). Does Azure Marketplace allow Redwood to set a floor price for the bundle that differs from standalone SKU list prices? We need to ensure the reseller margin math doesn't push us below our committed effective price.

2) Channel margin reconciliation: For our reseller (Cloudwave), they expect a 15% pass-through margin on any Azure Private Offer. We want to confirm if you are able to (a) honor a 15% channel pass-through within the PO, and (b) provide an auditable breakdown (list price, private-offer discount, reseller margin) in the invoice/settlement so our finance team can reconcile spend.

If you can share a sample private-offer structure or a quick matrix showing list price vs PO net vs reseller pass-through, that would help speed approvals.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Head of Cloud Procurement | IronBank Analytics

---
Attachment: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@ironbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Question on Azure bundle thresholds + partner margin

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details below:

• Yes — you can set a bundle list price that is independent from standalone SKU list prices on Azure Marketplace (we often do this for product packs).
• We can accommodate a 15% reseller pass-through in the Private Offer cadence, but there are two things we need to align on: (1) where margins are expressed (PO net vs marketplace settlement) and (2) rounding/tax handling that affects the final net.

I attached a lightweight pricing model (pricing_model_v3.xlsx) and a sample private-offer PDF that shows how we map list/PO/net/reseller-passback. The workbook includes a scenario tab for a 1-year commit at two volume tiers and shows effective price per token after a 15% reseller pass-through.

Key implementation notes:
- For the bundle floor price: we set the bundle list price in your publisher listing; Azure supports listing-override for bundled offers. We recommend holding standalone SKUs at the published list so channel math remains predictable.
- For the reseller pass-through: we can encode the pass-through as a documented "reseller fee" line in the PO and reflect it in our invoice memo. Marketplaces differ on whether that fee is passed through in marketplace settlement vs direct invoicing — for Azure Private Offers the simplest is to include the pass-through as a line in the PO.
- For auditability: we can provide a two-line settlement stub (list price / PO discount) and a reconciliation CSV at month-end for the first 3 months as part of the onboarding.

Next steps I propose: Ben (CC) to confirm the exact numbers for the tiered commit matrix and any reserved capacity uplift. Laura will coordinate finance billing fields we should include in the PO for your AP team.

If that works, I can convert the workbook into your preferred format and propose a draft PO template for review by EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Sales Manager, Strategic Marketplaces | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Turnkey LLM inference for production

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), azure_private_offer_template.pdf (PDF)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@ironbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on Azure bundle thresholds + partner margin

Marta / Naomi — quick note from the pricing side.

We reviewed the two-tier proposal Naomi attached. For the 1-year commit scenarios, the arithmetic on the attached sheet yields the following effective ranges (post 15% reseller pass-through):
- Volume Tier A (0–5M tokens/month): effective $0.00095–$0.00105 per token
- Volume Tier B (5M+ tokens/month): effective $0.00068–$0.00080 per token

A couple of operational caveats to flag:
1) Azure sometimes enforces a minimum listing (list price) that interacts oddly with per-unit meter pricing; if you plan to anchor the bundle list price significantly below standalone list price, we should flag Marketplace Ops to avoid auto-normalization.
2) Tax and VAT handling can change the net by ~1–3% depending on bill-to country — we can model that into the PO if you share the billing address.
3) If Cloudwave expects the 15% as a line-item, we prefer it be documented as "reseller fee" in the PO; we cannot show both a PO-level reseller line and a separate invoice-level passback without double-count risk.

I'll be available on Friday afternoon for a 30-min call if IronBank wants to walk through the workbook row-by-row.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Marketplace Pricing | Redwood Inference
